label: TP
reason: Both alerts are true positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) has user input flowing directly to the sink expression at L61-L62 ('... + ...') within the SQL string construction, bypassing the switch logic which only selects between literals or the original param. The resolved sink value is attacker-controlled. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) correctly identifies user input reaching the SQL query string at L56. The switch statement does not mitigate XSS risk because the vulnerable path (cases C/D) allows param to flow unchanged to the sink.

evidence.note: User input flows to SQL injection point (L56) and XSS sink (L61-62) via param -> bar -> sql concatenation.
